judgment.notes: M001 is applied once with scalar ℝ, Euclidean V=ℝ^m, ξ=t, f=g equal to the explicitly extended time section, and both derivative vectors ut(x,t). The named Euclidean structures discharge its structural premises. H002 at the interior point gives both HasDerivAt premises; BG001–BG008 check the smooth-section restriction, derivative identification and locality. The extension has value u(x,t) since t>0. The real inner-product conclusion is exactly the derivative used in S001; finite dot symmetry gives twice u·ut. H004 is used only on positive times, so q need not have unit norm. BG010 converts H004's unit norm to this self-dot identity. M001 yields derivative ut·u+u·ut=2u·ut; BG008–BG009 give derivative zero of the same function and BG011 checks uniqueness. The real scalar 2 is nonzero, hence F001. In S002 H005 supplies a real a at this same point. In coordinates, ut·(a u)=Σ_i ut_i(a u_i)=aΣ_i ut_i u_i=a(u·ut)=0 by F001. This needs no regularity of a and is exactly the second identity. Arbitrary positive t excludes the only extension boundary; neither n nor m needs positivity, and no global boundedness, limit exchange or spatial differentiation rule is used.
